segments.text:
Here Nebuchadnezer doth confeſſe that the Mages were called in vayne. Whereby it appeareth that all their knowledge was deceiuable: or at ye leaſt that Daniel could expounde the dreame that came not by mans ſtudy or induſtry, but by an heauenly reuelation. And I do embrace this ſentence, that Nebuchadnezer would expreſſe plainly that Daniel was taught by God to interprete dreames, & that this was a ſingular gift of his ſpirite. For he doubted not but that if there were any arte of diuination, his Mages, enchaunters, and Chaldees which boaſted vpon the title of perfect knowledge, had it. This then was without controuerſie with him, that they knew all thinges that man could know, and ſeyng they could not know this thyng, it appeared that Daniel was taught of God, and ſo Nebuchadnezer did extoll him aboue all the Mages, as though he ſhould
ſay that he was a Prophet from heauen, as appeareth afterward.
